'''Malabika Pramanik''' is a Canadian mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of British Columbia]]. Her interests include [[harmonic analysis]], [[complex variable]]s, and [[partial differential equation]]s.

== Education and career ==
Pramanik studied statistics at the [[Indian Statistical Institute]], earning a bachelor's degree in 1993 and a master's in 1995. She then moved to the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where she completed a doctorate in mathematics in 2001.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Weighted Integrals in <math>\mathbb{R}^2</math> and the Maximal Conjugated Calderon–Zygmund Operator'', was supervised by [[F. Michael Christ]].{{r|mgp}} After short-term positions at the [[University of Wisconsin]], [[University of Rochester]], and [[California Institute of Technology]], she joined the UBC faculty in 2006.{{r|cv}}  She was appointed director of the [[Banff International Research Station]] in 2020.{{r|birs}} In 2025, she was elected vice president of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. <ref>{{cite web |title=American Mathematical Society Election Results |url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/elections/election-results |website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Pramanik is the 2015–2016 winner of the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]]  of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]],{{r|michler}} and
the 2016 winner of the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]], given annually by the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] to an outstanding female researcher in mathematics.{{r|cornell}}
In 2018 the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] listed her in their inaugural class of fellows.{{r|cmsf}} She was named a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], in the 2022 "for contributions to complex and harmonic analysis and mentoring and support for the participation of under-represented groups in mathematics"{{r|fams}}. Pramanik was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2022{{r|icm}}.
